source.text: וּבַשָּׁנָ֨ה הַשְּׁבִעִ֜ית הִתְחַזַּ֣ק יְהוֹיָדָ֗ע וַיִּקַּ֣ח אֶת־שָׂרֵ֣י הַמֵּא֡וֹת לַעֲזַרְיָ֣הוּ בֶן־יְרֹחָ֡ם וּלְיִשְׁמָעֵ֣אל בֶּן־יְ֠הוֹחָנָן וְלַֽעֲזַרְיָ֨הוּ בֶן־עוֹבֵ֜ד וְאֶת־מַעֲשֵׂיָ֧הוּ בֶן־עֲדָיָ֛הוּ וְאֶת־אֱלִישָׁפָ֥ט בֶּן־זִכְרִ֖י עִמּ֥וֹ בַבְּרִֽית׃

records.literal_gloss: And in the year the seventh strengthened himself Jehoiada and took the commanders of the hundreds, Azariah son of Jeroham and Ishmael son of Jehohanan and Azariah son of Obed and Maaseiah son of Adaiah and Elishaphat son of Zichri, with him in covenant.

en.L: And in the seventh year Jehoiada strengthened himself and took the commanders of hundreds, Azariah son of Jeroham and Ishmael son of Jehohanan and Azariah son of Obed and Maaseiah son of Adaiah and Elishaphat son of Zichri, [into] a covenant with him.
en.B: In the seventh year Jehoiada took courage. He brought the commanders of hundreds into a covenant with him: Azariah son of Jeroham, Ishmael son of Jehohanan, Azariah son of Obed, Maaseiah son of Adaiah and Elishaphat son of Zichri.
en.R: In the seventh year Jehoiada the priest found the courage to act. He made a covenant with the commanders who each led a hundred men. They were Azariah son of Jeroham, Ishmael son of Jehohanan, Azariah son of Obed, Maaseiah son of Adaiah and Elishaphat son of Zichri.

decisions.choice: 2 Kings 11:4-20 tells the same events; Chronicles names the commanders
decisions.reason: Verses 1-21 retell 2 Kings 11:4-20, often in the same words, and the wording here follows that chapter wherever the Hebrew is the same. Each difference is noted at its verse. Here Kings says that Jehoiada "sent and took the commanders of hundreds of the Carites and of the runners" and brought them into the temple; Chronicles says that he "strengthened himself", names five commanders, and does not mention the Carites or the runners.

decisions.choice: strengthened himself: took courage and acted firmly
decisions.reason: The verb form means to make oneself strong, to take courage for a hard task (2 Chronicles 1:1; 15:8). After six years of hiding the boy, Jehoiada now moves against Athaliah.

decisions.choice: took ... with him in covenant: bound them to himself by a covenant
decisions.reason: "Took" governs the five names, and "with him in covenant" says how: he made them parties to a sworn agreement with him, as in 2 Kings 11:4.

decisions.choice: commanders of hundreds: officers each over a unit of about a hundred men
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 11:4. The army and the guard were organized in units of thousands, hundreds, fifties and tens (1 Samuel 22:7).

decisions.choice: the priest; who each led a hundred men
decisions.reason: Readable says who Jehoiada was (verse 8; 22:11) and explains "commanders of hundreds", as in 2 Kings 11:4.

decisions.choice: took courage (Balanced); found the courage to act (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of "strengthened himself" (m2).

source.text: וַיָּסֹ֨בּוּ֙ בִּֽיהוּדָ֔ה וַיִּקְבְּצ֤וּ אֶת־הַלְוִיִּם֙ מִכָּל־עָרֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה וְרָאשֵׁ֥י הָאָב֖וֹת לְיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ אֶל־יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And they went around in Judah and gathered the Levites from all [the] cities of Judah and [the] heads of the fathers of Israel, and they came to Jerusalem.

en.L: And they went around in Judah and gathered the Levites from all the cities of Judah and the heads of the fathers' [houses] of Israel, and they came to Jerusalem.
en.B: They went throughout Judah and gathered the Levites from all the towns of Judah and the heads of families of Israel, and they came to Jerusalem.
en.R: They traveled all through Judah and gathered the Levites from every town, along with the family leaders of Israel. Then they all came to Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: the Levites and the heads of the fathers' houses gathered from all Judah: not in Kings
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 11 has nothing like this verse. There Jehoiada works with the officers of the royal guard; Chronicles shows the Levites and the family heads of the whole nation drawn into the plan, so that the crowning is the act of the whole assembly (verse 3).

decisions.choice: the heads of the fathers: the leaders of the ancestral families
decisions.reason: "Fathers" here is short for "fathers' houses", the extended families that made up a tribe (1 Chronicles 24:4). Their heads were the leading men of each family.

decisions.choice: Israel: the people of God gathered in Judah
decisions.reason: The heads of families come from the towns of Judah, but Chronicles calls them "of Israel", the name of the whole covenant people (2 Chronicles 11:3; 12:6).

decisions.choice: heads of the fathers' [houses] (Literal); heads of families (Balanced); family leaders (Readable)
decisions.reason: As elsewhere in Chronicles (1 Chronicles 24:4, 6). Literal supplies "houses" in brackets (m2).

source.text: וַיִּכְרֹ֨ת כָּל־הַקָּהָ֥ל בְּרִ֛ית בְּבֵ֥ית הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים עִם־הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָהֶ֗ם הִנֵּ֤ה בֶן־הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ יִמְלֹ֔ךְ כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה עַל־בְּנֵ֥י דָוִֽיד׃

records.literal_gloss: And made all the assembly a covenant in [the] house of the God with the king. And he said to them, Look, [the] son of the king will reign, as spoke Yahweh concerning [the] sons of David.

en.L: And all the assembly made a covenant in the house of God with the king. And he said to them, "Look, the son of the king shall reign, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke concerning the sons of David.
en.B: In the house of God the whole assembly made a covenant with the king. Jehoiada said to them, "Here is the king's son! He shall reign, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} promised concerning the descendants of David.
en.R: There in God's temple the whole gathering made a covenant with the king. Jehoiada said to them, "Look, this is the king's son. He must be king, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} promised about David's descendants.

decisions.choice: the whole assembly makes a covenant with the king: Kings has Jehoiada and the commanders
decisions.reason: In 2 Kings 11:4 Jehoiada makes a covenant with the commanders, puts them under oath and shows them the king's son. Chronicles has the whole assembly make a covenant with the king himself, and gives Jehoiada's words about the promise to David, which Kings does not have.

decisions.choice: as Yahweh spoke concerning the sons of David: the promise of a lasting dynasty
decisions.reason: Yahweh had promised David that his descendants would sit on his throne (2 Samuel 7:12-16; 1 Chronicles 17:11-14; 2 Chronicles 21:7). Athaliah's attempt to wipe out the royal line (22:10) set itself against that promise; the hidden boy is its proof.

decisions.choice: with the king; the son of the king: Joash
decisions.reason: The boy Joash is already called "the king" before he is crowned. "The son of the king" is the son of the dead King Ahaziah.

decisions.choice: the assembly: the gathered people
decisions.reason: The assembly is the gathering of verse 2: the Levites and the family heads with the commanders, the people assembled before God.

decisions.choice: promised
decisions.reason: "Spoke concerning" here means a promise Yahweh made (m2); Balanced and Readable say so.

decisions.choice: Jehoiada
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the speaker, which the Hebrew leaves as "he".

source.text: זֶ֥ה הַדָּבָ֖ר אֲשֶׁ֣ר תַּעֲשׂ֑וּ הַשְּׁלִשִׁ֨ית מִכֶּ֜ם בָּאֵ֣י הַשַּׁבָּ֗ת לַכֹּֽהֲנִים֙ וְלַלְוִיִּ֔ם לְשֹֽׁעֲרֵ֖י הַסִּפִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: This [is] the thing which you will do: the third of you, [those] coming in [on] the sabbath, of the priests and of the Levites, [as] gatekeepers of the thresholds,

en.L: This [is] the thing that you shall do: the third of you who come in on the sabbath, of the priests and of the Levites, [shall be] gatekeepers of the thresholds,
en.B: Here is what you must do. One third of you who come on duty on the sabbath, priests and Levites, will be gatekeepers at the doorways,
en.R: Here is what you must do. The priests and Levites who come on duty on the sabbath will be divided into three groups. One group will be gatekeepers at the temple doors.

decisions.choice: the same order as 2 Kings 11:5, given to priests and Levites
decisions.reason: The opening words are those of 2 Kings 11:5. There the men coming on duty are the royal guard and the first third keeps watch over the palace; here they are priests and Levites, and the first third guards the thresholds of the temple.

decisions.choice: coming in on the sabbath: coming on duty when the shifts changed
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 11:5. The priests and Levites served in divisions that changed on the sabbath (1 Chronicles 9:25), so on that day the outgoing and incoming groups were both at the temple (verse 8).

decisions.choice: the third of you: the men on duty are split into three groups
decisions.reason: One third guards the thresholds, one the palace and one the Foundation Gate (verse 5), while the people stay in the courts. Chronicles sets out the division more plainly than 2 Kings 11:5-7.

decisions.choice: gatekeepers of the thresholds: guards at the temple entrances
decisions.reason: The thresholds are the doorways of the temple (2 Kings 12:10; 1 Chronicles 9:19). The Levite gatekeepers had charge of them; here a third of those on duty guard them.

decisions.choice: will be divided into three groups. One group; temple
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the division into three that verses 4-5 imply (m3), as in 2 Kings 11:5, and says which doors are meant (m4).

source.text: וְהַשְּׁלִשִׁית֙ בְּבֵ֣ית הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְהַשְּׁלִשִׁ֖ית בְּשַׁ֣עַר הַיְס֑וֹד וְכָל־הָעָ֔ם בְּחַצְר֖וֹת בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: and the third at [the] house of the king, and the third at [the] gate of the Foundation; and all the people in [the] courts of [the] house of Yahweh.

en.L: and the third at the house of the king, and the third at the Gate of the Foundation; and all the people [shall be] in the courts of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: one third will be at the king's palace, and one third at the Foundation Gate. All the people will be in the courts of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: Another group will be at the king's palace, and the third group at the Foundation Gate. All the people will stay in the courtyards of the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: Kings has the Sur Gate and the gate behind the runners; Chronicles adds the people in the courts
decisions.reason: In 2 Kings 11:5-6 the three groups guard the palace, the Sur Gate and the gate behind the runners. Chronicles has the palace and the Foundation Gate, and adds that all the people are to stay in the courts of the temple.

decisions.choice: the Gate of the Foundation: a gate whose site is unknown
decisions.reason: This gate is named only here. It stands where 2 Kings 11:6 has "the gate of Sur"; in Hebrew the two names differ by little more than one letter.

decisions.choice: all the people in the courts: the crowd stays outside the temple building
decisions.reason: The people gathered from Judah (verse 2) wait in the open courts. Only priests and Levites may go into the house itself (verse 6).

decisions.choice: Another group; the third group
decisions.reason: Readable continues the three groups it named in verse 4.

source.text: וְאַל־יָב֣וֹא בֵית־יְהוָ֗ה כִּ֤י אִם־הַכֹּֽהֲנִים֙ וְהַמְשָׁרְתִ֣ים לַלְוִיִּ֔ם הֵ֥מָּה יָבֹ֖אוּ כִּי־קֹ֣דֶשׁ הֵ֑מָּה וְכָל־הָעָ֔ם יִשְׁמְר֖וּ מִשְׁמֶ֥רֶת יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And let not come [into the] house of Yahweh except the priests and the [ones] ministering of the Levites; they will come, for holiness they [are]; and all the people will keep [the] charge of Yahweh.

en.L: And let no one come into the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} except the priests and those of the Levites who minister; they may come in, for they [are] holy; and all the people shall keep the charge of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Let no one enter the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} except the priests and the Levites who minister there. They may enter, because they are holy, but all the people must keep the charge of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: No one is to go into the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} except the priests and the Levites who are on duty. They may go in because they are holy. All the people must do what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} requires and stay outside.

decisions.choice: only priests and ministering Levites may enter, for they are holy: Kings has the guard
decisions.reason: In 2 Kings 11:7 the two companies going off duty, soldiers of the guard, keep watch over the house of Yahweh for the king, and Kings has spoken of the Carites and the runners. Chronicles says instead: let no one enter the house of Yahweh except the priests and the ministering Levites, for they are holy. In Chronicles the guard inside the temple is made up of those who may lawfully be there.

decisions.choice: they are holy: set apart for service in the sanctuary
decisions.reason: The priests and Levites had been set apart for the work of Yahweh's house (Numbers 3:5-10; 18:1-7; 1 Chronicles 23:28-32). Others who came near the holy place were to die (Numbers 1:51; 18:7).

decisions.choice: keep the charge of Yahweh: do what Yahweh requires
decisions.reason: The phrase means to carry out a duty Yahweh has laid down (Leviticus 8:35; Numbers 9:19). Here the people's part is to stay in the courts and not enter the house.

decisions.choice: those of the Levites who minister: the Levites on duty
decisions.reason: The participle means those serving at the temple, the Levites whose turn it was.

decisions.choice: do what the LORD requires and stay outside
decisions.reason: Readable explains "keep the charge" and says what it means for the people here (m3).

source.text: וְהִקִּיפוּ֩ הַלְוִיִּ֨ם אֶת־הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ סָבִ֗יב אִ֚ישׁ וְכֵלָ֣יו בְּיָד֔וֹ וְהַבָּ֥א אֶל־הַבַּ֖יִת יוּמָ֑ת וִֽהְי֥וּ אֶת־הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ בְּבֹא֥וֹ וּבְצֵאתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And will surround the Levites the king all around, each man and his weapons in his hand, and the [one] coming into the house will be put to death; and be with the king in his coming in and in his going out.

en.L: And the Levites shall surround the king all around, each man with his weapons in his hand, and whoever comes into the house shall be put to death; and be with the king when he comes in and when he goes out."
en.B: The Levites are to surround the king on every side, each man with his weapons in hand. Anyone who comes into the house must be put to death. Stay with the king wherever he goes."
en.R: The Levites must form a circle around the king, every man holding his weapons. Anyone else who comes into the temple must be killed. Stay close to the king wherever he goes."

decisions.choice: the Levites surround the king; whoever enters the house: Kings has the guards and the ranks
decisions.reason: The words are those of 2 Kings 11:8 with three differences. In Kings the guards surround the king; here it is the Levites. In Kings anyone who "comes into the ranks" is to die; here anyone who "comes into the house". And Kings says "going out and coming in", Chronicles "coming in and going out".

decisions.choice: whoever comes into the house: anyone not allowed to enter
decisions.reason: After verse 6 this means anyone other than the priests and Levites who tries to enter the temple, who would be a threat to the king.

decisions.choice: when he comes in and when he goes out: wherever he goes
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 11:8. Coming in and going out together cover all of a person's movements (Deuteronomy 28:6).

decisions.choice: the orders end here
decisions.reason: Jehoiada's words that began in verse 3 end with this verse; verse 8 tells how they were carried out.

decisions.choice: wherever he goes
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 11:8, Balanced and Readable give the sense of the idiom (m3).

decisions.choice: Anyone else
decisions.reason: Readable adds "else" to show that the priests and Levites are not meant (m2).

source.text: וַיַּעֲשׂ֨וּ הַלְוִיִּ֜ם וְכָל־יְהוּדָ֗ה כְּכֹ֣ל אֲשֶׁר־צִוָּה֮ יְהוֹיָדָ֣ע הַכֹּהֵן֒ וַיִּקְחוּ֙ אִ֣ישׁ אֶת־אֲנָשָׁ֔יו בָּאֵ֣י הַשַּׁבָּ֔ת עִ֖ם יוֹצְאֵ֣י הַשַּׁבָּ֑ת כִּ֣י לֹ֥א פָטַ֛ר יְהוֹיָדָ֥ע הַכֹּהֵ֖ן אֶת־הַֽמַּחְלְקֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And did the Levites and all Judah according to all that commanded Jehoiada the priest, and took each his men, [those] coming in [on] the sabbath with [those] going out [on] the sabbath, for not had dismissed Jehoiada the priest the divisions.

en.L: And the Levites and all Judah did according to all that Jehoiada the priest had commanded, and each took his men, those coming in on the sabbath with those going out on the sabbath, for Jehoiada the priest had not dismissed the divisions.
en.B: The Levites and all Judah did everything Jehoiada the priest had ordered. Each brought his men, both the ones who came on duty on the sabbath and the ones who went off duty that day, for Jehoiada the priest had not released the divisions.
en.R: The Levites and all the people of Judah did just what Jehoiada the priest told them. Each leader brought his men, both those who were starting their duty on the sabbath and those who were finishing it. Jehoiada the priest had not let any of the groups go home.

decisions.choice: the Levites and all Judah; the divisions not dismissed: Kings has the commanders
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 11:9 says that "the commanders of hundreds" did as Jehoiada commanded and came to him. Chronicles says "the Levites and all Judah", and adds the reason both shifts were there: Jehoiada had not dismissed the divisions.

decisions.choice: the divisions: the groups of priests and Levites who served by turns
decisions.reason: David had arranged the priests and Levites in divisions that took turns at the temple (1 Chronicles 23:6; 24:1-19). By keeping the outgoing division at the temple, Jehoiada doubled the number of men on hand.

decisions.choice: both shifts together
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 11:9: the men coming on duty and those going off duty were both present.

decisions.choice: Each leader; go home
decisions.reason: Readable says who brought the men and what being "dismissed" would have meant.

source.text: וַיִּתֵּן֩ יְהוֹיָדָ֨ע הַכֹּהֵ֜ן לְשָׂרֵ֣י הַמֵּא֗וֹת אֶת־הַֽחֲנִיתִים֙ וְאֶת־הַמָּגִנּוֹת֙ וְאֶת־הַשְּׁלָטִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֖ר לַמֶּ֣לֶךְ דָּוִ֑יד אֲשֶׁ֖ר בֵּ֥ית הָאֱלֹהִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And gave Jehoiada the priest to [the] commanders of the hundreds the spears and the shields and the shields which [were] to the king David, which [were in the] house of the God.

en.L: And Jehoiada the priest gave to the commanders of hundreds the spears and the bucklers and the shields that [had belonged] to King David, which [were in] the house of God.
en.B: Jehoiada the priest gave the commanders of hundreds the spears and the two kinds of shields that had belonged to King David and were kept in the house of God.
en.R: Jehoiada the priest handed out to the commanders the spears and shields that had belonged to King David. They were kept in God's temple.

decisions.choice: Jehoiada named; spears plural; a second word for shields; the house of God
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 11:10 says "the priest gave ... the spear and the shields that had belonged to King David, which were in the house of Yahweh". Chronicles names Jehoiada, has the plural "spears", adds a second word for shields, and says "the house of God".

decisions.choice: bucklers and shields: two kinds of shield
decisions.reason: The first word is the common round shield carried by a soldier. The second is the rare word of 2 Kings 11:10, used for the gold pieces David took from Hadadezer's officers (2 Samuel 8:7); it was most likely a kind of shield, though some take it as quivers.

decisions.choice: David's weapons in the temple: trophies kept at the house of God
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 11:10. Weapons won in battle were kept in a sanctuary as a sign of victory (2 Samuel 8:7, 11). Arming the guard with David's weapons tied the new king to David's line.

decisions.choice: the bucklers and the shields (Literal); the two kinds of shields (Balanced); shields (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the two words apart, with "shields" for the word used in 2 Kings 11:10; Balanced says there were two kinds; Readable simply says "shields".

source.text: וַיַּעֲמֵ֨ד אֶת־כָּל־הָעָ֜ם וְאִ֣ישׁ׀שִׁלְח֣וֹ בְיָד֗וֹ מִכֶּ֨תֶף הַבַּ֤יִת הַיְמָנִית֙ עַד־כֶּ֤תֶף הַבַּ֨יִת֙ הַשְּׂמָאלִ֔ית לַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ וְלַבָּ֑יִת עַל־הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ סָבִֽיב׃

records.literal_gloss: And he stationed all the people, and each [had] his weapon in his hand, from [the] side of the house the right to [the] side of the house the left, by the altar and by the house, by the king all around.

en.L: And he stationed all the people, each man with his weapon in his hand, from the right side of the house to the left side of the house, by the altar and by the house, around the king on every side.
en.B: He stationed all the people, each man with his weapon in hand, from the south side of the temple to the north side, beside the altar and the temple, surrounding the king.
en.R: He put all the people in their places, each man holding his weapon. They formed a line from the south side of the temple to the north side, near the altar and the temple building, to surround and protect the king.

decisions.choice: Jehoiada stations all the people: in Kings the runners take their places
decisions.reason: The words follow 2 Kings 11:11, where "the runners stood, each man with his weapons in his hand". In Chronicles Jehoiada stations "all the people", and the word for weapon is a different one (m3).

decisions.choice: right side, left side: south side, north side
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 11:11. Directions were named facing east, the way the temple faced, so "right" is south and "left" is north.

decisions.choice: his weapon: a hand weapon, perhaps a javelin
decisions.reason: This word for a weapon is less common than the general word in verse 7. It may name a spear or javelin, or any weapon in general (Nehemiah 4:11, 17).

decisions.choice: the altar and the house: the court in front of the temple
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 11:11. The altar for burnt offerings stood in the court before the temple building, where the king would be shown.

decisions.choice: south side; north side
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the compass directions that "right" and "left" mean here (m2).

decisions.choice: to surround and protect the king
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 11:11, Readable adds "protect" to make the purpose clear (verse 7).

source.text: וַיּוֹצִ֣יאוּ אֶת־בֶּן־הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ וַיִּתְּנ֤וּ עָלָיו֙ אֶת־הַנֵּ֨זֶר֙ וְאֶת־הָ֣עֵד֔וּת וַיַּמְלִ֖יכוּ אֹת֑וֹ וַיִּמְשָׁחֻ֨הוּ֙ יְהוֹיָדָ֣ע וּבָנָ֔יו וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ יְחִ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And they brought out the son of the king and put on him the crown and the testimony, and made king him; and anointed him Jehoiada and his sons, and said, may live the king.

en.L: And they brought out the son of the king and put on him the crown and the testimony, and they made him king; and Jehoiada and his sons anointed him, and they said, "May the king live!"
en.B: Then they brought out the king's son and put on him the crown and the testimony. They made him king, and Jehoiada and his sons anointed him and shouted, "Long live the king!"
en.R: Then they brought out the king's son. They put the crown on him and the testimony, and made him king. Jehoiada and his sons poured olive oil on his head, and they shouted, "Long live the king!"

decisions.choice: the testimony: probably a written copy of Yahweh's covenant law
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 11:12. The word is used for the covenant law, especially the tablets kept in the ark (Exodus 25:16, 21). The king was to have his own copy of the law (Deuteronomy 17:18-19), and this may be what was given to Joash at his crowning. Because Saul's crown is paired with an armband in 2 Samuel 1:10, and the two Hebrew words look alike, some think this was a royal ornament rather than a document.

decisions.choice: they brought out; Jehoiada and his sons anointed him; no clapping
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 11:12 has "he brought out" and "they anointed him", and adds that the people clapped their hands. Chronicles has "they brought out", names Jehoiada and his sons, priests, as the ones who anointed the king, and does not mention the clapping.

decisions.choice: may the king live: the acclamation of a new king
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 11:12. This is the cry with which the people welcomed a new king (1 Samuel 10:24; 1 Kings 1:39).

decisions.choice: the crown: the sign of a consecrated ruler
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 11:12. The word names the royal crown (2 Samuel 1:10) and also the high priest's holy diadem (Exodus 29:6).

decisions.choice: Long live the king!
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 11:12, Balanced and Readable use the familiar English acclamation; Literal keeps the Hebrew form.

decisions.choice: the testimony
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 11:12, every level keeps "testimony", the singular used for the covenant tablets, because the sense here is uncertain (m1).

decisions.choice: poured olive oil on his head
decisions.reason: Readable explains what anointing is, as in 2 Kings 11:12.

source.text: וַתִּשְׁמַ֣ע עֲתַלְיָ֗הוּ אֶת־ק֤וֹל הָעָם֙ הָֽרָצִ֔ים וְהַֽמְהַֽלְלִ֖ים אֶת־הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַתָּב֥וֹא אֶל־הָעָ֖ם בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And heard Athaliah the sound of the people, the [ones] running and the [ones] praising the king, and came to the people [to the] house of Yahweh.

en.L: And Athaliah heard the sound of the people running and praising the king, and she came to the people [in] the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: When Athaliah heard the noise of the people as they ran and praised the king, she went to the people at the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: Athaliah heard the noise of the people running and cheering for the king. So she went to the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, where the people were.

decisions.choice: the people running and praising the king: Kings has the runners and the people
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 11:13 has "the sound of the runners, the people", the guards and the crowd. Chronicles has "the sound of the people running and praising the king": the word for the guards becomes people running, and the praise of the king is added.

decisions.choice: praising the king: acclaiming him
decisions.reason: The verb is the usual word for praise. Here it is the crowd's shouts in honor of the new king (verse 11).

decisions.choice: she came to the people: Athaliah goes into the temple court
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 11:13. She came into the place where the guard had been set (verses 4-10).

decisions.choice: cheering for
decisions.reason: Readable uses an everyday word for the people's praise of the king (m2).

source.text: וַתֵּ֡רֶא וְהִנֵּ֣ה הַמֶּלֶךְ֩ עוֹמֵ֨ד עַֽל־עַמּוּד֜וֹ בַּמָּב֗וֹא וְהַשָּׂרִ֣ים וְהַחֲצֹצְרוֹת֮ עַל־הַמֶּלֶךְ֒ וְכָל־עַ֨ם הָאָ֜רֶץ שָׂמֵ֗חַ וְתוֹקֵ֨עַ֙ בַּחֲצֹ֣צְר֔וֹת וְהַמְשֽׁוֹרֲרִים֙ בִּכְלֵ֣י הַשִּׁ֔יר וּמוֹדִיעִ֖ים לְהַלֵּ֑ל וַתִּקְרַ֤ע עֲתַלְיָ֨הוּ֙ אֶת־בְּגָדֶ֔יהָ וַתֹּ֖אמֶר קֶ֥שֶׁר קָֽשֶׁר׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And she looked, and look, the king [was] standing by his pillar at the entrance, and the commanders and the trumpets [were] by the king, and all [the] people of the land [were] rejoicing and blowing on trumpets, and the singers with [the] instruments of the song and leading [in] praise; and tore Athaliah her clothes and said, Conspiracy, conspiracy.

en.L: And she looked, and look, the king [was] standing by his pillar at the entrance, and the commanders and the trumpets [were] beside the king, and all the people of the land [were] rejoicing and blowing on trumpets, and the singers with the instruments of song [were] leading the praise; and Athaliah tore her clothes and said, "Treason! Treason!"
en.B: She looked, and there was the king, standing by his pillar at the entrance, with the commanders and the trumpeters beside him. All the people of the land were rejoicing and blowing trumpets, and the singers with their musical instruments were leading the praise. Athaliah tore her clothes and cried out, "Treason! Treason!"
en.R: She looked and saw the new king standing by his pillar at the entrance. The commanders and the trumpet players were next to him. All the people of the land were celebrating and blowing trumpets. The singers were playing their instruments and leading the people in praise. Athaliah tore her clothes and screamed, "Treason! Treason!"

decisions.choice: his pillar at the entrance; the singers leading the praise: not in Kings
decisions.reason: The verse follows 2 Kings 11:14 with three differences. Kings has the king "by the pillar according to the custom"; Chronicles has "by his pillar at the entrance". Chronicles adds the singers with instruments of song leading the praise. And where Kings says Athaliah "called out", Chronicles has "said".

decisions.choice: his pillar at the entrance: the king's place at the temple
decisions.reason: The king had a set place by a pillar at the entrance of the temple court, where he stood on public occasions (2 Kings 11:14; 23:3). The text does not say whether it was one of the two bronze pillars of the porch (1 Kings 7:21) or a raised stand.

decisions.choice: the singers with the instruments of song: the Levite musicians
decisions.reason: David had appointed Levites to sing and play at the house of Yahweh (1 Chronicles 15:16; 25:1-7). Their praise turned the crowning into an act of worship.

decisions.choice: leading the praise: directing the people's praise
decisions.reason: The verb means to make known; here the singers give the signal for the praise and lead it.

decisions.choice: treason: a conspiracy against the ruler
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 11:14. The word means a plot; repeated, it is a cry of alarm. Athaliah calls the crowning of David's heir a plot against her.

decisions.choice: the trumpeters (Balanced); the trumpet players (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 11:14, Balanced and Readable say who stood by the king; Literal keeps "trumpets".

decisions.choice: Treason! Treason!
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 11:14: "treason" gives the sense of a plot against the throne in a short cry.

decisions.choice: cried out (Balanced); screamed (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has the plain "said" (m1); Balanced and Readable use the words of 2 Kings 11:14, since the words are a cry of alarm.

source.text: וַיּוֹצֵא֩ יְהוֹיָדָ֨ע הַכֹּהֵ֜ן אֶת־שָׂרֵ֥י הַמֵּא֣וֹת׀פְּקוּדֵ֣י הַחַ֗יִל וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲלֵהֶם֙ הֽוֹצִיא֨וּהָ֙ אֶל־מִבֵּ֣ית הַשְּׂדֵר֔וֹת וְהַבָּ֥א אַחֲרֶ֖יהָ יוּמַ֣ת בֶּחָ֑רֶב כִּ֚י אָמַ֣ר הַכֹּהֵ֔ן לֹ֥א תְמִית֖וּהָ בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And brought out Jehoiada the priest the commanders of the hundreds, [the] appointed ones of the army, and said to them, Bring her out to from between the ranks, and the [one] coming after her will be put to death with [the] sword; for had said the priest, Not you shall put her to death [in the] house of Yahweh.

en.L: And Jehoiada the priest brought out the commanders of hundreds, the officers of the army, and said to them, "Bring her out between the ranks, and whoever comes after her shall be put to death with the sword." For the priest had said, "You shall not put her to death [in] the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."
en.B: Jehoiada the priest brought out the commanders of hundreds who were in charge of the troops and said to them, "Bring her out between the ranks, and anyone who follows her is to be put to death with the sword." For the priest had said, "Do not put her to death in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."
en.R: Jehoiada the priest sent out the commanders in charge of the soldiers. He said to them, "Take her out between your lines, and kill anyone who follows her." He said this because he did not want her killed in the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: brought out: Jehoiada sent the commanders forward
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 11:15 has "commanded". The Chronicles verb means "brought out", perhaps that Jehoiada called the officers out from their posts to deal with Athaliah. The two Hebrew verbs look somewhat alike, and some think one has been copied from the other.

decisions.choice: the same orders as 2 Kings 11:15, with small differences
decisions.reason: Besides "brought out" (m1), Chronicles has "shall be put to death" where Kings has "put to death" as an order, and the priest's words are "You shall not put her to death" where Kings has "Let her not be put to death".

decisions.choice: out between the ranks: out through the lines of guards
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 11:15. She is to be led out under guard; the phrase may also mean "out of the temple precincts".

decisions.choice: not in the house of Yahweh: the temple must not be defiled by her death
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 11:15. Killing in the holy place would defile it (verse 19).

decisions.choice: the appointed ones of the army: the officers in charge of the troops
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 11:15, the phrase describes the commanders of hundreds; it is not a second group.

decisions.choice: He said this because he did not want her killed
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 11:15, Readable turns the priest's reported words into a statement of his reason.

source.text: וַיָּשִׂ֤ימוּ לָהּ֙ יָדַ֔יִם וַתָּב֛וֹא אֶל־מְב֥וֹא שַֽׁעַר־הַסּוּסִ֖ים בֵּ֣ית הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיְמִית֖וּהָ שָֽׁם׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And they put to her hands, and she came to [the] entrance of [the] gate of the horses [of the] house of the king, and they put her to death there.

en.L: And they laid hands on her, and she came to the entrance of the Horse Gate of the house of the king, and they put her to death there.
en.B: They seized her, and when she came to the entrance of the Horse Gate at the king's palace, they put her to death there.
en.R: So they took hold of her and led her to the entrance of the Horse Gate at the palace. There they killed her.

decisions.choice: they laid hands on her: they seized her
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 11:16. The phrase most likely means that the guards took hold of her; it may also mean "they made way for her".

decisions.choice: the entrance of the Horse Gate; they put her to death
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 11:16 has "by the way of the entrance of the horses" and "she was put to death there". Chronicles names it "the Horse Gate" and says "they put her to death there".

decisions.choice: the Horse Gate of the king's house: a gate into the palace grounds
decisions.reason: This was the gate through which horses were brought into the royal grounds, outside the temple court. Jeremiah 31:40 and Nehemiah 3:28 name a Horse Gate in the city wall.

decisions.choice: led her
decisions.reason: Readable says that the guards took her to the gate.

source.text: וַיִּכְרֹ֤ת יְהוֹיָדָע֙ בְּרִ֔ית בֵּינ֕וֹ וּבֵ֥ין כָּל־הָעָ֖ם וּבֵ֣ין הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ לִהְי֥וֹת לְעָ֖ם לַיהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And made Jehoiada a covenant between himself and between all the people and between the king, to be as a people for Yahweh.

en.L: And Jehoiada made a covenant between himself and all the people and the king, that they should be a people for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Jehoiada made a covenant binding himself, all the people and the king to be the people of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: Then Jehoiada made a covenant that bound himself, all the people and the king together. They promised to belong to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: a covenant between Jehoiada, the people and the king: Kings has Yahweh and two covenants
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 11:17 has "the covenant between Yahweh and the king and the people", and a second covenant "between the king and the people". Chronicles has one covenant, "between himself and all the people and the king".

decisions.choice: to be a people for Yahweh: the heart of the covenant
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 11:17. This is the central promise of Yahweh's covenant with Israel (Exodus 6:7; Deuteronomy 26:18). After Athaliah's years of Baal worship, the people bind themselves to Yahweh again.

decisions.choice: between himself: Jehoiada as the priest who leads the covenant
decisions.reason: Jehoiada is one party to the covenant. As the priest of Yahweh he stands where Kings names Yahweh, and he binds the people and the king to Yahweh's service.

decisions.choice: They promised to belong to
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 11:17, Readable makes the people's promise a sentence of its own.

source.text: וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ כָל־הָעָ֤ם בֵּית־הַבַּ֨עַל֙ וַֽיִּתְּצֻ֔הוּ וְאֶת־מִזְבְּחֹתָ֥יו וְאֶת־צְלָמָ֖יו שִׁבֵּ֑רוּ וְאֵ֗ת מַתָּן֙ כֹּהֵ֣ן הַבַּ֔עַל הָרְג֖וּ לִפְנֵ֥י הַֽמִּזְבְּחֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And went all the people [to the] house of the Baal and pulled it down; and its altars and its images they broke, and Mattan, priest of the Baal, they killed before the altars.

en.L: And all the people went [to] the house of Baal and pulled it down; and its altars and its images they broke, and Mattan the priest of Baal they killed before the altars.
en.B: Then all the people went to Baal's house and tore it down. They smashed its altars and its images, and killed Mattan, Baal's priest, before the altars.
en.R: Then all the people went to Baal's temple and tore it down. They smashed its altars and idols. They killed Mattan, Baal's priest, in front of the altars.

decisions.choice: all the people; they broke: Kings has the people of the land and "broke thoroughly"
decisions.reason: The verse follows 2 Kings 11:18, where "all the people of the land" go to the house of Baal and "broke thoroughly" its altars and images. Chronicles says "all the people" and "they broke". Kings' last clause, about the guards set over the temple, is told at length in verses 18-19.

decisions.choice: the house of Baal: a temple of Baal in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 11:18. Baal worship came to Judah through the house of Ahab, to which Athaliah belonged (21:6; 22:2-3).

decisions.choice: Mattan: the priest of Baal
decisions.reason: Mattan is named only here and in 2 Kings 11:18. He was killed at his own altars.

decisions.choice: idols
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 11:18, Readable uses the plain word "idols".

source.text: וַיָּשֶׂם֩ יְהוֹיָדָ֨ע פְּקֻדֹּ֜ת בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֗ה בְּיַ֨ד הַכֹּהֲנִ֣ים הַלְוִיִּם֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָלַ֣ק דָּוִיד֮ עַל־בֵּ֣ית יְהוָה֒ לְֽהַעֲל֞וֹת עֹל֣וֹת יְהוָ֗ה כַּכָּת֛וּב בְּתוֹרַ֥ת מֹשֶׁ֖ה בְּשִׂמְחָ֣ה וּבְשִׁ֑יר עַ֖ל יְדֵ֥י דָוִֽיד׃

records.literal_gloss: And put Jehoiada [the] offices of [the] house of Yahweh in [the] hand of the priests the Levites whom had divided David over [the] house of Yahweh, to offer up burnt offerings of Yahweh as [is] written in [the] law of Moses, with joy and with song, by [the] hands of David.

en.L: And Jehoiada put the offices of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} into the hand of the priests the Levites, whom David had divided over the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, to offer the burnt offerings of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as [it is] written in the law of Moses, with rejoicing and with song, by the hands of David.
en.B: Jehoiada put the oversight of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in the hands of the Levitical priests, whom David had assigned in divisions over the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. They were to offer the burnt offerings of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as the law of Moses directs, with rejoicing and singing, as David had ordered.
en.R: Jehoiada put the Levitical priests in charge of the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. David had divided them into groups to serve there. They were to offer the burnt offerings to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, as the law of Moses says. They were to do it with joy and singing, in the way David had arranged.

decisions.choice: the offerings set in order as written in the law of Moses, with rejoicing and song, by the order of David: Kings has one clause
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 11:18 ends, "And the priest set appointed guards over the house of Yahweh." Chronicles uses the same word for "offices" and tells at length how Jehoiada restored the temple's order: the priests offering the burnt offerings as written in the law of Moses, with rejoicing and song, by the order of David.

decisions.choice: the offices: the duties of oversight at the temple
decisions.reason: The word means posts or duties of oversight. Here it covers the whole charge of the temple and its service, given back to those appointed for it.

decisions.choice: the priests the Levites: the priests of the tribe of Levi
decisions.reason: The phrase means the priests, who are Levites (Deuteronomy 17:9; 18:1). Some ancient translations read "the priests and the Levites", naming both groups.

decisions.choice: whom David had divided: the divisions of priests and Levites
decisions.reason: David had arranged the priests and Levites in divisions, each with its turn of service (1 Chronicles 23:6; 24:1-19).

decisions.choice: by the hands of David: as David had ordered
decisions.reason: "By the hands of" here means under the direction of someone (1 Chronicles 25:2, 6). The burnt offerings follow the law of Moses (Numbers 28-29); the singing follows the order David gave for the Levite musicians (1 Chronicles 16:4-6, 37-42).

decisions.choice: the Levitical priests
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of "the priests the Levites" (m3) in one phrase.

decisions.choice: David had divided them into groups ...; They were to do it with joy and singing
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the long Hebrew sentence into four short ones.

source.text: וַֽיַּעֲמֵד֙ הַשּׁ֣וֹעֲרִ֔ים עַֽל־שַׁעֲרֵ֖י בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה וְלֹֽא־יָבֹ֥א טָמֵ֖א לְכָל־דָּבָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And he stationed the gatekeepers at [the] gates of [the] house of Yahweh, and not would come [one] unclean in any thing.

en.L: And he stationed the gatekeepers at the gates of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, so that no one unclean in any matter should come in.
en.B: He stationed the gatekeepers at the gates of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, to keep out anyone who was unclean in any way.
en.R: He put gatekeepers at the gates of the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. They made sure that no one who was unclean for any reason could go in.

decisions.choice: the gatekeepers, so that no one unclean in anything should enter: not in Kings
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 11 has nothing like this verse. Chronicles adds that Jehoiada stationed the gatekeepers at the temple gates so that no one unclean in anything should enter, keeping the temple holy after the years of Athaliah.

decisions.choice: unclean: not ritually fit to come near the holy place
decisions.reason: Uncleanness came from things such as touching a dead body, certain diseases or bodily discharges (Leviticus 11-15; Numbers 19). An unclean person could not enter the sanctuary until made clean (Leviticus 7:20-21; Numbers 19:20).

decisions.choice: unclean in any matter: unclean for any reason
decisions.reason: The phrase covers every kind of uncleanness.

decisions.choice: the gatekeepers: the Levites who guarded the temple gates
decisions.reason: The gatekeepers were Levites who kept watch at the gates of the temple (1 Chronicles 9:17-27; 26:1-19).

source.text: וַיִּקַּ֣ח אֶת־שָׂרֵ֣י הַמֵּא֡וֹת וְאֶת־הָֽאַדִּירִים֩ וְאֶת־הַמּֽוֹשְׁלִ֨ים בָּעָ֜ם וְאֵ֣ת׀כָּל־עַ֣ם הָאָ֗רֶץ וַיּ֤וֹרֶד אֶת־הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ מִבֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֔ה וַיָּבֹ֛אוּ בְּתֽוֹךְ־שַׁ֥עַר הָֽעֶלְי֖וֹן בֵּ֣ית הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיּוֹשִׁ֨יבוּ֙ אֶת־הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ עַ֖ל כִּסֵּ֥א הַמַּמְלָכָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And he took the commanders of the hundreds and the nobles and the rulers over the people and all [the] people of the land, and brought down the king from [the] house of Yahweh, and they came through [the] middle of [the] gate the upper [to the] house of the king, and they seated the king on [the] throne of the kingdom.

en.L: And he took the commanders of hundreds and the nobles and the rulers over the people and all the people of the land, and he brought the king down from the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and they came through the Upper Gate [to] the house of the king; and they seated the king on the throne of the kingdom.
en.B: He took with him the commanders of hundreds, the nobles, the rulers over the people and all the people of the land. He brought the king down from the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. They went through the Upper Gate to the king's palace and seated the king on the royal throne.
en.R: Jehoiada gathered the commanders, the nobles, the leaders of the people and all the people of the land. Together they led the king down from the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. They went through the Upper Gate into the palace and placed the king on the royal throne.

decisions.choice: the nobles and rulers; the Upper Gate; the throne of the kingdom
decisions.reason: The verse follows 2 Kings 11:19 with differences. Kings names "the Carites and the runners" where Chronicles has "the nobles and the rulers over the people"; Kings has "by the way of the gate of the runners" where Chronicles has "through the Upper Gate"; and in Kings "he sat on the throne of the kings", where here "they seated the king on the throne of the kingdom".

decisions.choice: the nobles and the rulers over the people: the leading men of Judah
decisions.reason: The nobles are the powerful and honored men; the rulers are those with authority over the people. With the commanders and the people of the land, the whole nation takes part.

decisions.choice: the Upper Gate: a gate between the temple and the palace
decisions.reason: A gate of this name belonged to the temple; Jotham later built it (27:3). Through it the procession went down from the temple to the palace.

decisions.choice: brought the king down from the house of Yahweh: from the temple hill to the palace
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 11:19. The temple stood on higher ground than the palace.

decisions.choice: the royal throne
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 11:19, Balanced and Readable say "royal throne".

decisions.choice: Jehoiada
decisions.reason: Readable names Jehoiada as the one who led them.

source.text: וַיִּשְׂמְח֥וּ כָל־עַם־הָאָ֖רֶץ וְהָעִ֣יר שָׁקָ֑טָה וְאֶת־עֲתַלְיָ֖הוּ הֵמִ֥יתוּ בֶחָֽרֶב׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And rejoiced all [the] people of the land, and the city was quiet; and Athaliah they had put to death with the sword.

en.L: And all the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was quiet; and Athaliah they had put to death with the sword.
en.B: All the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was at peace. Athaliah had been put to death with the sword.
en.R: All the people of the land were happy, and the city was calm. Athaliah had been killed with a sword.

decisions.choice: the people rejoiced and the city was quiet
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 11:20. The people of Judah celebrate, and Jerusalem stays quiet, with no one rising to fight for Athaliah.

decisions.choice: Athaliah they had put to death: the story closes on her end
decisions.reason: The verb looks back to verse 15. Putting Athaliah's name first closes the story where it began (22:10).

decisions.choice: Kings adds "at the king's house"
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 11:20 ends "with the sword at the house of the king"; Chronicles ends with "the sword".

decisions.choice: was at peace (Balanced); was calm (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 11:20: the city was quiet, without disorder.
